evidence: heap.lisp:259-313 fnn-heap-operator-profile wraps the whole operator-plan, profile-resolve, connection-count and cold-resource resolution in `(handler-case ... (error () nil))`. fnn-heap-command-profile then reserves for `(values nil 0 ...)`, and fnn-command-heap prints the decision line with exit 0.
fix: Catch only the operator plan's semantic refusals (no profile, as documented). Let fnn-store-fault and other faults escape so the probe prints no line and the launcher reports a fault.
notes: 2026-10-03 codex-operator-retire: source repair connected to actual CLI/heap consumer and actual ACL2 closed failure classifier. SCN-1098 discriminates old actual heap (fault→acceptance) and old group encoder boundary (malformed→refusal). Known refusal preserved; generic/unlisted faults and uncertainty propagate with no accepting heap line. Source evidence archived operator-diagnostics-classification-2026-10-03.json; matching image remains Integration work. S090 also repaired nested store-profile blanket catch.
reviewer: fnn-heap-operator-profile wraps the whole operator-plan, profile and cold-resource resolution in (handler-case ... (error () nil)) (heap.lisp:259-313). That catches fnn-store-fault and guard errors from fnn-core along with the intended refusals, and fnn-command-heap then prints an accepting no-store reservation with ACL2's exit code (heap.lisp:347-361). The header's stated contract only distinguishes 'no line' from 'refused line', and the comment at 253-255 intends to swallow refusals only. Impact is limited because the exec'd node re-runs the same resolution and surfaces the fault itself, but the probe does report a fault as an acceptance.
scenario: For `fn operator CONFIG run`, a fault in fnn-operator-run-at, fn-bs-profile-resolve, or fn-native-operator-host-result-run-cold-resources (an ACL2 guard error, which fnn-call raises as fnn-store-fault) is not a refusal. It is silently turned into 'no profile'. The launcher receives an accepting `heap=` line sized for the no-store figure, without the store's profile or the cold-pool extension, and execs the node. The node then either refuses its own budget or runs under a reservation smaller than its profile needs. The heap.lisp header says a probe fault must never look like a decision.
title: The heap probe swallows any fault while resolving the operator profile and prints an accepting no-store heap line
